🐝Bee Fact Friday #10

Did you know bees visit around 4.4 million flowers to produce just 1 kg of honey? 

Each day, worker bees make 10–15 foraging flights, visiting 50–100 flowers per trip.

That means a single jar of honey is the result of thousands of bees working together.🌸 https://t.co/Ufo39ECAnP

Spraying pesticides while plants are in bloom can be fatal for bees, yet people still do it.

During flowering, bees collect nectar and pollen.

If pesticides are used at this stage, these substances contaminate the very resources bees depend on for food.

Research has shown that pesticide exposure can disrupt bee navigation, weaken immune systems, reduce reproduction, and lead to colony losses.

Because pollinators play a critical role in global food production and ecosystem stability, using pesticides during flowering periods while pollinators are actively foraging is illegal in many countries.

To truly protect bees, we must raise awareness and educate people about their importance.

🐝Bee Fact Friday #7

You’ve probably never seen a male honeybee.

A honeybee colony consists of about 95% female bees.

They take care of everything, from foraging and defending the hive to nursing the young and cleaning.

Male honeybees stay in the hive until they’re mature enough to join drone congregations. There, they gather at high altitudes and wait for a queen from another hive to mate.

Male bees don’t take part in the daily work of the colony like the workers do. Their main role is reproduction, while the female bees keep the colony running.

It’s a simple but fascinating system that keeps the hive healthy.👸

🐝Bee Fact Friday #5

A queen bee can live up to 5 years and lay over a million eggs in her lifetime, while worker bees live around 6 weeks in summer and are infertile.

The interesting part? They share the exact same DNA.

The only difference between them comes down to nutrition.

Worker larvae receive royal jelly produced by nurse bees for only the first three days, then switch to honey and pollen. 

A future queen, however, is fed royal jelly throughout her entire development.

That single dietary difference changes everything.

It extends her lifespan and shortens her development time from 21 days to just 16. 
She is also the largest, growing up to 60% larger than the rest of the colony.

Same DNA. Completely different destiny.

What we consume shapes what we become, that’s why HiveBits stands for 100% natural production.
